— Conversion optimization

Help more of the right visitors take the next step.

More traffic is not always the first thing a website needs. I review how visitors understand your offer, navigate the page, and complete important actions so that improvements address real sources of friction.

Discuss conversion optimization

A connected approach to conversion optimization

Conversion optimization combines evidence and clear design decisions. A visitor may hesitate because the offering is unclear, essential information is missing, the mobile layout is difficult, or the form asks for too much too soon. Some issues can be corrected directly; others require a hypothesis and a careful test. The goal is to make the journey more useful, not to pressure people into actions that are wrong for them.

When this work can help

  • Visitors reach key pages but rarely complete useful inquiries.
  • Landing pages do not match the message that brought people there.
  • Changes are made frequently without a clear baseline or test question.

How I approach the work

I review priority journeys, available analytics, the quality of inquiries, and the information visitors need to decide. Findings become a prioritized set of hypotheses with clear success measures and guardrails. Where traffic is insufficient for a reliable experiment, usability review and monitored improvements are more honest than claiming statistical proof from a small sample.

Core activities & deliverables

Journey and page audit

Inspect message clarity, visual hierarchy, navigation, form effort, mobile behavior, and common technical failures. Review the relationship between traffic intent and destination content.

Landing-page improvements

Clarify the offer, place useful evidence near decisions, simplify the next step, and address practical questions. Keep claims factual and avoid manipulative urgency or invented social proof.

Testing and learning

Define a primary metric, minimum meaningful effect, guardrails, and a stopping plan where an experiment is justified. Document results, including inconclusive outcomes and operational side effects.

Who this is for

Conversion work suits businesses with existing traffic and a meaningful action to improve, such as qualified inquiries, appointments, or purchases. It can begin with an audit when measurement is limited, but a tracking repair may be needed before evaluating results. Small businesses can benefit from simpler journeys even when traffic volumes do not support formal A/B testing.

What to consider before starting

A design change cannot compensate for every issue with demand, pricing, product fit, or follow-up. I do not claim conversion improvements that have not been measured. Test results are specific to a context and may not generalize. Changes affecting accessibility, lead quality, refunds, or customer trust need review even if a short-term completion rate rises.

How we assess progress

Choose the outcome that matters and keep supporting indicators separate. A form-start rate can reveal interest, but qualified inquiries are a more meaningful commercial measure. An experiment should monitor downstream quality and technical errors alongside its main metric. Reporting should distinguish observation, plausible explanation, and evidence strong enough to support a decision.

Questions about conversion optimization

Do we need A/B testing?+

Only when traffic, conversion volume, and the decision justify it. Direct usability fixes and measured releases can be more suitable for smaller sites.

Will you guarantee a conversion increase?+

No. The work identifies and tests improvements. Results depend on traffic, the offer, implementation, and other parts of the customer journey.
